publication: Trusted generation record stores a separate runtime inventory bound to canonical root and commit. Existing activation fingerprints, snapshot gates, intent/recovery and reader lifetime are preserved. Default scope covers every root file and directory except proven evidence/docs and Git administrative entry; dependencies are included.
loadingProof: Literal imports, dynamic imports, package targets, child script paths and URL package inputs must remain protected. Known nonliteral loaders have exact source digest proofs and explicit targets; TypeScript parser/scanner APIs have a library digest plus exact consumer digest proofs. Changed loaders/dependencies/consumers require a new reviewed proof and newly gated generation; runtime never repairs missing proof.
guard: Each origin verification enumerates and rehashes protected scopes and checks current paths, bytes, modes, canonical root and aliases. It does not traverse/stat/read excluded evidence/docs. Actual modules must be proven loading targets; retained readers use their own generation inventory.
compatibility: Older registry generations without runtimeInventory refuse production origin. There is no lazy upgrade or fallback full-tree success. New publication must create the inventory with the complete runtime tree and installed TypeScript 6.0.3; parser is lazy and not loaded by verify/origin.
